test.design_rationale: The client cannot pause the affiliate programme business-wide and cannot randomise buyers to treatment or control at the individual level from aggregated/indexed data. A matched_comparison is the strongest design the constraints allow: a client-nominated treatment set of products or regions has promotion depth reduced, while a matched comparison set of similar products or regions continues at current discount depth. Matching on prior-quarter GMV index, affiliate order index, and discount intensity index — using the same evidence series already supplied — gives the closest available like-for-like. This design can support medium confidence at best, consistent with the evidence grade rules. A split_test would require platform-level buyer randomisation that is not confirmed as available; a holdout would require withholding affiliate promotion entirely from a segment, which conflicts with the client's business constraint. matched_comparison is therefore the strongest honest choice. Test window to be agreed against the actual commercial calendar. Avoid major promotional, platform or seasonal events that would materially confound the read. Duration should be sufficient to produce a readable sample and should not be hard-coded before a real pilot is scoped. The primary volume read comes inside the window; the repeat read is directional only because of the long re-purchase cycle [ev_6].
test.treatment: On the client-nominated treatment set only: offer / discount depth on affiliate-attributed orders is reduced to one level approved by the client finance and commerce teams against their own margin recovery target. Nothing else changes: affiliate content approach, listing content, creator roster, media weight, price list, stock, SKU set, affiliate budget and other promotional mechanics are held as they are, and no new proof or content is added to the listing or the affiliate content. Treatment-set buyers are tagged in the CRM for repeat tracking.
test.comparison: A matched comparison set of products or regions of similar prior-quarter GMV index, affiliate order index, and discount intensity index, continuing to operate at current (unreduced) promotion depth and current affiliate incentive structure throughout the test window. This group is the stable baseline against which the treatment set's volume, margin, and conversion are read.

calendar_confounds.event: Commercial, platform and seasonal calendar (not supplied)
calendar_confounds.risk: A major promotional, platform or seasonal event touching either group could change traffic and volume independently of offer depth and swamp the read.
calendar_confounds.mitigation: Test window to be agreed against the actual commercial calendar. Avoid major promotional, platform or seasonal events that would materially confound the read. Duration should be sufficient to produce a readable sample and should not be hard-coded before a real pilot is scoped. Any unplanned event that hits either group makes the result inconclusive.

held_constant.item: Affiliate content approach and listing content
held_constant.how_verified: Execution owner supplies the current content brief at launch and confirms in writing each week that no new content direction, creative or listing proof was issued for either group; any change is logged as a confound.
Client commerce team confirms the list price on both groups is unchanged, and shares a weekly price-list check for the test window.

held_constant.item: Creator roster on the treatment set
held_constant.how_verified: Execution owner provides a named list of active affiliates at launch; any addition or removal is flagged immediately and logged against the test record.
Client commerce team confirms paid media spend and targeting on both groups are unchanged; any unplanned activation is logged and assessed.
Client commerce team confirms stock is sufficient on both groups; any stock-out is flagged, and the affected SKU or region is excluded from the final read.
Client commerce team fixes the SKU list for each group at launch; any addition or removal is logged and the SKU is excluded from the read.
Client commerce team confirms total affiliate spend is unchanged from its prior level; execution owner supplies a weekly spend report against the indexed baseline.

held_constant.item: Other promotional mechanics (vouchers, bundles, platform promotions) where feasible
held_constant.how_verified: Client commerce team shares a promotion log for both groups at launch and weekly; any change is logged and any mechanic that cannot be held is recorded as a deviation.

measures.label: Affiliate order volume: treatment vs matched comparison (relative difference)
measures.definition: The percentage difference in affiliate-attributed order volume on the treatment set (reduced promotion depth) relative to the matched comparison set (current promotion depth) over the test window. A result at or above the threshold indicates that volume has held within a commercially acceptable range despite the reduction in promotion depth — consistent with demand that is not primarily price-triggered. The proposed threshold of -10% is drawn from the falsification criterion stated in Stage 1 explanation E1 ('volume holds within a commercially acceptable range, e.g. less than 10% decline') and is proposed for client agreement before the test launches; it is not a prediction. The client finance and commerce teams should confirm whether a different tolerance is implied by the margin recovery target set for the test.
measures.failure_condition: The treatment set's affiliate order volume falls more than 10 percent below the matched comparison set's volume over the test window — consistent with demand being primarily price-triggered and the programme being structurally discount-dependent. This would support explanation E1 and indicate that scaling at reduced promotion depth would destroy volume.

measures.label: Gross margin index: treatment set compared with matched comparison set — must not be lower
measures.definition: The gross margin index on the treatment set (reduced offer depth) compared with the matched comparison set (current offer depth) over the test window, expressed as a relative difference. The test is designed to recover margin; this guardrail checks that the treatment set's gross margin is not lower than the matched comparison set's (for example, because returns, fulfilment costs or affiliate fee structures offset the discount reduction). A proposed threshold of 0 percent relative difference is set: the treatment set's gross margin must be at or above the matched comparison set's. This is the minimum condition for the test to be commercially meaningful; if gross margin on the treatment set falls below that of the matched comparison set, the intervention has not achieved its stated purpose.
measures.failure_condition: The treatment set's gross margin index is lower than the matched comparison set's gross margin index over the test window, meaning the offer-depth reduction has not recovered margin and the intervention has not delivered its primary commercial rationale.

measures.label: Discount intensity index on the treatment set: must be lower than matched comparison set
measures.definition: The discount intensity index on the treatment set relative to the matched comparison set over the test window. This guardrail verifies that the treatment was actually delivered as specified — i.e. that promotion depth on the treatment set was genuinely reduced and did not drift back toward the current level through affiliate-initiated vouchers, platform-run promotions, or other mechanisms. The guardrail passes if the treatment set's discount intensity index is strictly below the matched comparison set's index. A proposed threshold of -1 percent relative difference is set as the minimum detectable reduction; the client finance and commerce teams should confirm the actual intended reduction depth before the test launches.
measures.failure_condition: The treatment set's discount intensity index is not materially below the matched comparison set's index — meaning the promotion-depth reduction was not delivered as specified, and any volume or margin result cannot be attributed to the treatment. The test result is inconclusive and the treatment delivery must be investigated before any decision is made.

measures.label: Repeat purchase rate index on the treatment set: must not fall below matched comparison set
measures.definition: The repeat purchase rate index on the treatment set (buyers acquired at reduced promotion depth) relative to the matched comparison set (buyers acquired at current promotion depth) over the test window and the subsequent quarter. Given the long re-purchase cycle noted in ev_6, a single-quarter read is acknowledged as insufficient to conclude on loyalty; this guardrail is therefore set as a directional floor — the treatment set's repeat rate must not fall below the matched comparison set's repeat rate. A proposed threshold of 0 percent relative difference is set: the treatment set's repeat index must be at or above the matched comparison set's. A result below this threshold would be consistent with the treatment acquiring lower-loyalty buyers even at reduced discount depth, which would be a negative signal for the reshape strategy.
measures.failure_condition: The treatment set's repeat purchase rate index falls below the matched comparison set's repeat rate index over the observation window — consistent with reduced-discount buyers being less likely to return, which would undermine the case for reshaping the programme toward lower-discount mechanics. Note: given the long re-purchase cycle (ev_6), a single-quarter read should be treated as directional only and not as a confirmed loyalty failure.

signals.success: The treatment set's affiliate order volume holds within 10 percent of the matched comparison set (primary measure passes); the treatment set's gross margin index is at or above the matched comparison set's (margin guardrail passes); the treatment set's discount intensity index is materially below the matched comparison set's (confirming treatment delivery); and the treatment set's repeat rate index is at or above the matched comparison set's (repeat guardrail passes). All held-constants verified as unchanged throughout the test window. This pattern is consistent with demand on the treatment set not being primarily price-triggered, and would support a decision to reshape the affiliate programme toward lower-discount mechanics before scaling budget.
signals.failure: The treatment set's affiliate order volume falls more than 10 percent below the matched comparison set (primary measure fails) — regardless of whether margin recovers. This pattern is consistent with demand being primarily price-triggered on the treatment set, and would support a decision to reframe the board's scale ambition against a margin-adjusted growth target rather than scaling the current discount-led structure. A failure on the margin guardrail alone (volume holds but margin does not recover) would indicate that the discount reduction is being offset by other cost or incentive mechanisms and the intervention design requires revision before any scale decision.
signals.inconclusive: The result should be treated as inconclusive — and the test repeated or redesigned — in any of the following conditions: (1) the matched comparison set is found not to be sufficiently similar to the treatment set on prior-quarter GMV, affiliate order, or discount intensity indices; (2) total volume across both groups is too small to produce a readable relative difference at the proposed threshold; (3) any held-constant is found to have changed during the test window (affiliate content approach, listing content, price list, SKU set, media weight, stock, creator roster, affiliate budget, other promotional mechanics); (4) the discount intensity guardrail shows the treatment was not delivered as specified; (5) a platform-wide sale event (or any unplanned promotional, platform or seasonal event) occurs during the test window and affects either group; (6) the new-versus-repeat customer split (ev_9) or promo-versus-full-price order mix (ev_8) remain unavailable at the time of result read, preventing interpretation of what the volume result means for demand quality.

decision_rule.statement: A clean pass requires all of the following to hold simultaneously: (1) the primary measure — affiliate order volume on the treatment set — is within 10 percent of the matched comparison set (gte -10%); (2) the gross margin index on the treatment set is at or above the matched comparison set (gte 0% relative difference); (3) the discount intensity index on the treatment set is materially below the matched comparison set (lte -1% relative difference), confirming treatment delivery; (4) the repeat purchase rate index on the treatment set is at or above the matched comparison set (gte 0% relative difference); (5) all held-constants — affiliate content approach, listing content, price list, SKU set, media weight, stock, creator roster, affiliate budget, other promotional mechanics — are verified as unchanged throughout the test window; and (6) the treatment was delivered as specified with no routing errors, stock-outs, or unplanned platform events affecting either group. If any one of these conditions is not met, the result is not a clean pass and the decision owner should not treat it as a basis for scaling or reshaping the programme without further investigation.
